angle: What age protection the Twenty-sixth Amendment added

items.claim: Congress passed the amendment on March 23, 1971, and it was ratified on July 1, 1971.
items.synthesisExcerpt: Congress passed the amendment on March 23, 1971, and it was ratified on July 1, 1971.
items.sourceEvidence: Archives.gov source, as provided in the operator paraphrase: Congress passed the amendment on March 23, 1971, and it was ratified on July 1, 1971.
items.qualification: Context only; does not define the age protection.

items.claim: The amendment protects citizens aged 18 or older from age-based voting-rights restrictions by both federal and state governments.
items.synthesisExcerpt: The amendment bars both federal and state governments from denying or limiting US citizens' voting rights because of age when the citizens are at least 18.
items.sourceEvidence: Archives.gov source, as provided in the operator paraphrase: the amendment bars federal and state governments from denying or limiting US citizens' voting rights because of age when they are at least 18.
items.usefulness: States the amendment's central age-based protection and who it binds.
items.qualification: Applies to US citizens at least 18; the stated bar concerns restrictions because of age.

items.claim: Congress may enforce the amendment through appropriate legislation.
items.synthesisExcerpt: Congress can enforce the amendment through appropriate legislation.
items.sourceEvidence: Archives.gov source, as provided in the operator paraphrase: Congress can enforce the amendment through appropriate legislation.
items.usefulness: Adds the stated mechanism for congressional enforcement.
items.qualification: The synthesis does not specify what legislation Congress may enact.
